messages.subject: Big O and Simmer?
parts:
How should we approach a project in Simmer from the perspective of performance and Big O?  Is the length of the event list the n?  No big rush on this question, but some thoughts would be helpful as I'm conceptualizing bigger projects.

“The time will come when diligent research over long periods will bring to light things which now lie hidden."

Seneca the Younger

messages.author: 57ddef5748efce88
messages.subject: Re: Big O and Simmer?
parts:
Very interesting question and dependent on a huge number of factors. Take for example a trajectory function that is passed a function x; function x can be "hard" to calculate (it could in theory even contain an NP-hard computation on its own). 

Realising that I didn't give an answer to your question: this makes me think that we should have some standard problem definitions to test on. This would allow to track the evolution of simmer's performance on these definition over time (for new version of simmer)

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Big O and Simmer?
parts: The complexity of a simulation model has nothing to do with the event queue. The event queue is a working abstraction totally transparent for and independent of the system you are modelling. The complexity of a model emerges from the number of steps that the underlying algorithm requires. If you ignore user-embedded functions, then the complexity is related to the trajectory, to the number of activities.
